The original homeland of the Slavs was probably located somewhere in Eastern and Central Europe, and from there they gradually migrated in different directions. Over time, they became divided into three major groups: Western Slavs, Eastern Slavs and Southern Slavs. The Western Slavs included the ancestors of modern Poles, Czechs and Slovaks, as well as several groups that later disappeared or were assimilated. The Eastern Slavs became the ancestors of modern Russians, Ukrainians and Belarusians, while the Southern Slavs included Serbs, Croats, Slovenes, Bulgarians, Macedonians, Montenegrins and Bosnians. During the 7th century, one of the first larger Slavic political organizations appeared under the leadership of Samo, a Frankish merchant who united several Slavic tribes and created a state that existed for several decades. In the 9th century, another important Slavic state appeared: Great Moravia. It became one of the most important political and cultural centers of the Slavic world. During the reign of Prince Rastislav, the Byzantine missionaries Cyril and Methodius arrived in Great Moravia in 863. They helped spread Christianity among the Slavs and created the Glagolitic script, while their followers later contributed to the development of the Cyrillic tradition. Their mission had an enormous influence on the culture and religion of many Slavic peoples, particularly in Eastern and Southeastern Europe. At the same time, the First Bulgarian Empire became one of the strongest states in Southeastern Europe. Bulgaria was founded in the 7th century and gradually became heavily Slavicized. In 864, under Boris I, Bulgaria officially adopted Christianity. During the reign of Simeon the Great in the late 9th and early 10th centuries, Bulgaria reached the height of its power and became an important political and cultural center. Bulgarian scholars and religious figures played an important role in spreading Slavic literacy and Christianity throughout the Balkans and the Eastern Slavic world. In Eastern Europe, another major Slavic state was developing: Kievan Rus'. Centered around Kyiv, it became one of the most powerful states in Eastern Europe during the 9th to 11th centuries. Important rulers included Oleg, Igor, Olga, Sviatoslav, Vladimir the Great and Yaroslav the Wise. One of the most important events in the history of the Eastern Slavs happened in 988, when Vladimir the Great adopted Christianity from the Byzantine Empire and introduced it to Kievan Rus'. This event shaped the religious and cultural development of the territories that later became Russia, Ukraine and Belarus. Under Yaroslav the Wise, Kievan Rus' reached one of its cultural and political peaks, but after his death the state gradually became divided between different princes and territories. In Central Europe, the Polish state began to develop around the Piast dynasty. The most important early ruler was Mieszko I, who accepted Christianity in 966. The Christianization of Poland connected the country more closely with Western Europe and strengthened its political position. His son, Bolesław I the Brave, continued expanding the state and was crowned king in 1025. Poland later experienced periods of political fragmentation, especially after the division of the country into several duchies, but it was eventually reunified. In the 14th and 15th centuries, Poland became increasingly powerful, especially after its union with Lithuania. mentions.title: Ear Seeding, kökleri Geleneksel Çin Tıbbı'na dayanan ve auriküloterapi (kulak akupunkturu) prensibiyle çalışan iğnesiz bir akupresür yöntemidir. Geleneksel tıbba göre kulak, tüm vücudun, organların ve sinir sisteminin bir mikrosistem haritasını taşır. Bu yöntemde iğne kullanılmaz; bunun yerine Vaccaria bitkisinin doğal tohumları, küçük metal küreler (genellikle altın, gümüş veya paslanmaz çelik) ya da kristaller cilde yapışan küçük medikal bantlar yardımıyla kulağın belirli refleks noktalarına yerleştirilir. Nasıl Çalışır? Yerleştirilen tohumlar kulaktaki belirli sinir uçlarına ve akupunktur noktalarına hafif, sürekli bir baskı uygular. Gün içinde kişinin bu noktalara parmaklarıyla hafifçe masaj yapması baskıyı artırarak etkiyi uyarır. Bu uyarılar; vagus siniri ve merkezi sinir sistemi üzerinden beyne sinyaller göndererek vücudun kendi kendini regüle etme mekanizmalarını harekete geçirir. Uygulama ve Kullanım Süresi Cilt alkolle temizlenip kurutulduktan sonra cımbız yardımıyla hedeflenen noktalara yapıştırılır. Genellikle 3 ila 5 gün boyunca kulakta kalır; duş alma veya günlük aktiviteler sırasında su geçirmez bantları sayesinde yerinde durur. Süre sonunda çıkarılır, kulak derisi birkaç gün dinlendirildikten sonra ihtiyaç duyulursa işlem tekrarlanır. not: tıbbi tanı ve teşhis içermez bilgilendirme amaçlıdır . . . . #çintıbbı #yüzyogası #yüzyogası #yuzyogasi #mewing

mentions.text:
Reply to lilwallywalrus's comment
How to mew
STEP 1
-PLACE TIP OF THE TONGUE BEHIND FRONT TEETH
STEP 2
-PRESS THE REST OF THE TONGUE TO THE ROOF OF YOUR MOUTH
TIP (make "NGG" sound)
(imagine Pressing the ROOT OF YOUR TONGUE to the roof as a support beam for your midface)
STEP 3
-REST TEETH TOGETHER SLIGHTLY & CLOSE LIPS
LASTLY,
-SWALLOW SPIT/SALIVA
SWALLOW SWALLOW SWALLOW
PROPER TONGUE POSTURE
VS
ACTIVELY
MEWING

mentions.title: Tongue posture can play a role in breathing, swallowing, and oral function, but there is currently little evidence supporting the idea that consciously suctioning your tongue to the roof of your mouth all day will reshape your face or improve TMJ symptoms. In some cases, forcing tongue posture may even create unnecessary tension in the tongue, jaw, and surrounding muscles!
